text:
maria: FYI BrightRoute (dedicated eu-west) reporting intermittent 429s + p99 latency spikes. They say their pool is "flapping" — scale up then down every few minutes. Can someone triage?

deploy-bot: [alert] autoscale-flapping detected for pool=dedicated-eu-west-brightroute metric=pgpu_utilization flaps=6 window=20m
josh: I'll grab graphs. quick look: CPU/GPU oscillation, scale events roughly every 2-4m. current autoscale cooldown=60s, target_util=70%.
josh: snippet from scaler logs:```
2026-03-15T10:15:02Z scale_up pool=dedicated-eu-west-brightroute from=8 to=12 reason=util>target
2026-03-15T10:17:50Z scale_down pool=dedicated-eu-west-brightroute from=12 to=9 reason=util<target
2026-03-15T10:20:40Z scale_up pool=dedicated-eu-west-brightroute from=9 to=13 reason=burst
```
lara: Customer attached a curl that reproduces 429s:```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"long prompt..."}'
``` They see ~30% of requests 429 during the flaps.
kai: throwaway hypothesis: noisy tenant doing large embedding/batch jobs causing GPU mem pressure -> OOM or cache eviction -> util drops and then spikes as processes restart. I see a tenant in the same pool running large batches around the same times. GPU driver logs show a few "CUDA out of memory" and eviction messages.
josh: metrics: p99 token latency spikes 2.8s -> 3.2s during spike, then drops to 180ms after scale down. The scaler might be overshooting because short cooldown allows it to react to transient traffic.
maria: can we reproduce in staging? if noisy neighbor is the root, need rate limit / isolation change and maybe longer cooldown.
kai: repro cmd in staging:```
python tools/load_test.py --pool dedicated-eu-west-brightroute-staging --rps 40 --seq 1024 --batch 128 --duration 10m
``` that simulates the large-batch tenant. observed: GPU memory climbs, OOM, fallback tasks to CPU -> latency and then scaler steps in.
josh: short-term mitigation: increase autoscale cooldown to 300s for this pool and set min_instances=10 to avoid undershooting during bursts. will also add a cool-down hysteresis: require util>target for 90s continuous before scale_up. planning to apply now.
kai: applied changes: cooldown=300s, min_instances=10, hysteresis_window=90s. pinned config at 10 instances temporarily. rolling config patch deployed.
maria: after change (30m) metrics update: p99 down to 420ms, 429s dropped to single-digit occurrences. still seeing embedding job at ~70% of GPU mem but no OOMs.
lara: told BrightRoute we've applied temporary mitigation and are investigating noisy tenant. they want credits for the downtime window.
abby: I'll open billing adjustment ticket and note mitigation window 2026-03-15T10:05->2026-03-15T11:00.
josh: root cause hypothesis: coworker tenant running large embedding batches with poor batching knobs causing memory thrash; autoscaler reacts to noisy short-term signals because cooldown/hysteresis were too low. two part fix: (1) longer default cooldowns for dedicated pools with mixed tenants; (2) noisy-tenant detector that auto-drains or throttles offending jobs.
maria: action items: 1) SRE: keep pool pinned for 24h and monitor 2) infra: build noisy-tenant detection rule + auto-throttle RFC 3) product: offer brighter isolation guidance to Dedicated customers. I'll schedule a follow-up with BrightRoute for postmortem on Tue.
kai: I'll capture driver logs and tenant job details and add to the incident folder.
lara: BrightRoute accepted temporary mitigation and asked for timeline on a permanent fix.
maria: thanks all. created a quick retro note and will add graph snapshots. tagging @kai @josh for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
